title.zh: 卷一百八十五 列傳第七十二: 呂思誠 汪澤民 干文傳 韓鏞 李稷 蓋苗
title.en: Volume 185 Biographies 72: Lu Sicheng, Wang Zemin, Gan Wenchuan, Han Yong, Li Ji, Gai Miao
title.raw: 卷一百八十五 列傳第七十二: 呂思誠 汪澤民 干文傳 韓鏞 李稷 蓋苗 Volume 185 Biographies 72: Lu Sicheng, Wang Zemin, Gan Wenchuan, Han Yong, Li Ji, Gai Miao

sentences.zh: 呂思誠

translations.literal: Lu Sicheng
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sicheng

sentences.zh: 呂思誠，字仲實，平定州人。

translations.literal: Lu Sicheng, style name Zhongshi, was a native of Pingding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sicheng, whose style was Zhongshi, came from Pingding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六世祖宗禮，金進士，遼州司戶。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zongli was a Jin dynasty jinshi and Household Registrar of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his ancestor Zongli had passed the Jin civil examination and served as household registrar of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 宗禮生仲堪，亦舉進士。

translations.literal: Zongli begot Zhongkan, who also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zongli's son Zhongkan also became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 仲堪生時敏，時敏生釗，為千夫長，死國事。

translations.literal: Zhongkan begot Shimin; Shimin begot Zhao, who was a chiliarch and died in service to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan's son Shimin had a son Zhao, a chiliarch who died in the state's service.

sentences.zh: 釗生德成，德成生允，卒平定知州致仕，思誠父也。

translations.literal: Zhao begot Decheng; Decheng begot Yun, who died in retirement as prefect of Pingding—he was Sicheng's father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son Decheng had a son Yun, who ended his days as retired prefect of Pingding; he was Sicheng's father.

sentences.zh: 母馮氏，夢一丈夫，烏巾、白襴衫、紅鞓束帶，趨而揖曰：「我文昌星也。」

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Feng, dreamed of a man in a black kerchief, white ramie shirt, and red sash who hurried forward, bowed, and said, "I am the Wenchang Star."
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Feng dreamed of a man in a black headcloth, white ramie shirt, and red sash who came forward, bowed, and said, "I am the Wenchang star."

sentences.zh: 及寤，思誠生，目有神光，見者異之。

translations.literal: When she awoke, Sicheng was born; his eyes shone with a strange light, and those who saw him were struck as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When she woke, Sicheng was born. His eyes held an uncanny gleam, and everyone who saw him thought it remarkable.

sentences.zh: 及長，從蕭㪺學治經。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he studied the classics under Xiao 㪺.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up, he studied the classics under Xiao 㪺.

sentences.zh: 已而入國子學為陪堂生，試國子伴讀，中其選。

translations.literal: Thereafter he entered the Directorate of Education as an attendant student, tested for companion reader of the Directorate, and was selected.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered the Directorate of Education as an attendant student, sat for the companion-reader examination, and passed.

sentences.zh: 擢泰定元年進士第，授同知遼州事，未赴。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the jinshi degree in the first year of Taiding, appointed Associate Administrator of Liaozhou, and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taiding reign he took the jinshi degree and was appointed associate administrator of Liaozhou, but never went to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 改景州蓨縣尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Tiao County in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Tiao County in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 差民戶為三等，均其徭役；

translations.literal: He classified households into three grades and equalized their corvée and tax levies;
translations.idiomatic: He divided households into three grades and equalized their labor and tax burdens;

sentences.zh: 刻孔子像，令社學祀事；

translations.literal: he had an image of Confucius carved and ordered village schools to perform sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: he had a statue of Confucius carved and ordered the village schools to maintain sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 每歲春行田，樹畜勤敏者，賞以農器，人爭趨事，地無遺力。

translations.literal: each spring he inspected the fields, and those diligent in planting trees and raising livestock were rewarded with farm tools; people vied to work, and not a patch of land was left untilled.
translations.idiomatic: each spring he toured the fields and rewarded those diligent in planting and stock-raising with farm tools; people rushed to do the work, and no land was left idle.

sentences.zh: 民石安兒等，流離積年，至是，聞風復業。

translations.literal: Among the people, Shi An'er and others had been displaced for years; now, hearing of his reputation, they returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Shi An'er and others among the people had been uprooted for years; now, hearing of his reforms, they came home and took up their trades again.

sentences.zh: 印識文簿，畀社長藏之，季月報縣，不孝弟、不事生業者，悉書之，罰其輸作。

translations.literal: He printed registers with official seals and gave them to village heads to keep; each season they reported to the county, and those unfilial, unbrotherly, or idle in their livelihoods were all recorded and fined with labor service.
translations.idiomatic: He printed sealed registers for village heads to keep; each quarter they reported to the magistrate, and anyone unfilial, unbrotherly, or neglecting his livelihood was recorded and fined with corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 胥吏至社者，何人用飲食若干，多者責償其直。

translations.literal: When clerks came to the villages, whoever had been fed and how much was recorded; if the amount was excessive, they were made to repay its value.
translations.idiomatic: When yamen clerks visited a village, every meal they took was logged; if the tally was too high, the clerk had to pay it back.

sentences.zh: 豪猾者竄名職田戶，思誠盡祛其弊。

translations.literal: The powerful and crafty had slipped their names onto the rolls of official-field households; Sicheng rooted out these abuses entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful schemers had slipped their names onto the rolls of official-field households; Sicheng swept those abuses away.

sentences.zh: 天歷兵興，豫貸鈔於富民，令下造軍器，事皆先集，民用不擾。

translations.literal: When war broke out in the Tiansli reign, he advanced paper money in advance to wealthy households and ordered them to manufacture arms; all tasks were gathered first, and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in the Tiansli era, he advanced paper notes to wealthy households and ordered them to forge weapons; everything was ready ahead of time, and ordinary people were left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 於後得官價，亟以還民。

translations.literal: Later, when official prices were received, he hurried to repay the people.
translations.idiomatic: When official reimbursement finally arrived, he paid the people back at once.

sentences.zh: 翟彝自其大父因河南亂，被掠為人奴，歲納丁粟以免作。

translations.literal: Zhai Yi, from his grandfather's time because of chaos in Henan, had been seized and made someone's slave; each year he paid grain as household tax to be exempted from labor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Yi's grandfather, caught up in the chaos in Henan, had been seized and enslaved; each year Yi paid grain as a quit-rent to avoid corvée.

sentences.zh: 思誠知彝力學，如其主與之約，終彝身粟三十石，仍代之輸，彝得為良民。

translations.literal: Sicheng knew that Yi studied hard; he made an agreement with Yi's master that for the rest of Yi's life thirty shi of grain would be paid, and Sicheng still paid it on his behalf; Yi was able to become a good commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how hard Zhai Yi studied, Sicheng struck a deal with his master: thirty shi of grain for the rest of Yi's life, which Sicheng himself paid; Yi was restored to free status.

sentences.zh: 他日買羊，劉智社民李，持酒來見，訴其弟匿羊，思誠叱之退。

translations.literal: Another day he bought a sheep; Li of Liuzhi community, holding wine, came to see him and accused his younger brother of hiding the sheep; Sicheng rebuked him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he bought a sheep. A man named Li from Liuzhi village came with wine, accused his brother of hiding the animal, and Sicheng drove him off with a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 王青兄弟四人，友愛彌篤，思誠至其家，取酒勸酬，歡同骨肉。

translations.literal: Wang Qing and his four brothers were deeply affectionate; Sicheng went to their home, took wine, and urged them to drink together, joyous as flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qing and his four brothers were devoted to one another. Sicheng visited their home, shared wine with them, and urged them on until they were as close as kin.

sentences.zh: 李之兄弟相謂曰：「我等終不敢見尹矣。」

translations.literal: The Li brothers said to one another, "We shall never dare face the magistrate again."
translations.idiomatic: The Li brothers said to each other, "We will never dare face the magistrate again."

sentences.zh: 各具酒食相切責，悔前過，析居三十年，復還同爨。

translations.literal: Each prepared food and drink and rebuked one another, regretting their former faults; though they had lived apart for thirty years, they returned to a single hearth.
translations.idiomatic: They each brought food and wine, scolded one another, and repented of their old quarrel; after thirty years of separate households, they moved back under one roof.

sentences.zh: 鎮民張復，叔母孀居，且瞽，丐食以活，恐思誠聞之，即日迎養。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu of the garrison town had a widowed, blind aunt who begged for food to live; fearing Sicheng would hear of it, he welcomed and supported her that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu of the garrison had a widowed, blind aunt who lived by begging; afraid Sicheng would learn of it, he took her in to support her the same day.

sentences.zh: 思誠憐其貧，令為媒互人以養之。

translations.literal: Sicheng pitied his poverty and had him made a marriage broker to support her.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying his poverty, Sicheng appointed him a marriage broker so he could support her.

sentences.zh: 天旱，道士持青蛇，曰盧師谷小青，謂龍也，禱之即雨。

translations.literal: In drought, a Daoist held a green snake, saying the Little Green of Lushi Valley was a dragon; if one prayed to it, rain would come.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought a Daoist paraded a green snake, claiming that Little Green of Lushi Valley was a dragon and that praying to it would bring rain.

sentences.zh: 思誠以其惑人，殺蛇，逐道士，雨亦隨至，遂有年。

translations.literal: Sicheng, because he was deluding the people, killed the snake and expelled the Daoist; rain followed at once, and the year turned abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng judged that he was misleading the people, killed the snake, and drove the Daoist away; rain came immediately, and the year ended in plenty.

sentences.zh: 縣多淫祠，動以百餘計，刑牲以祭者無虛日，思誠悉命毀之，唯存江都相董仲舒祠。

translations.literal: The county had many illicit shrines, often numbering over a hundred; not a day passed without slaughtering animals for sacrifice; Sicheng ordered them all destroyed, keeping only the shrine of Dong Zhongshu, Chancellor of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The county abounded in illicit shrines—often more than a hundred—with sacrifices and slaughter almost every day. Sicheng had them all torn down, sparing only the shrine to Dong Zhongshu, chancellor of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林國史院檢閱官，俄升編修。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Reviewing Officer of the Hanlin Academy and National History Office; soon he was advanced to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reviewing officer in the Hanlin Academy and National History Office, and soon advanced to compiler.

sentences.zh: 文宗在奎章閣，有旨取國史閱之，左右舁匱以往，院長貳無敢言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong was at the Kui Zhang Pavilion, there was an order to fetch the national history for reading; attendants carried the chests there, and neither the director nor the deputy dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wenzong was at the Kui Zhang Pavilion, an order went out to bring the national history for him to read. Attendants carried the chests over, and neither the director nor his deputy dared object.

sentences.zh: 思誠在末僚，獨跪閣下爭曰：「國史紀當代人君善惡，自古天子無觀閱之者。」

translations.literal: Sicheng, though a junior officer, alone knelt below the pavilion and protested: "The national history records the good and evil of the reigning ruler; from antiquity no Son of Heaven has been allowed to read it."
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng, though only a junior officer, knelt alone beneath the pavilion and protested: "The national history records the virtues and faults of the reigning sovereign. Since antiquity no emperor has been permitted to read it."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋擢國子監丞，升司業，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then advanced to Vice Chancellor, and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Directorate of Education, then vice chancellor, and finally investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 與斡玉倫徒等劾中書平章政事徹里帖木兒變亂朝政，章上，留中不下，思誠納印綬殿前，遂出僉廣西廉訪司事。

translations.literal: Together with Wo Yuluntu and others he impeached the Central Secretariat Grand Councillor Cherig Temur for throwing the court into disorder; the memorial went up, was held in the palace and not issued, and Sicheng surrendered his seal and ribbon before the throne; he was then sent out as Administrator of the Guangxi Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: With Wo Yuluntu and others he impeached Grand Councillor Cherig Temur of the Central Secretariat for wrecking the government. The memorial reached the throne but was held back. Sicheng laid his seal and ribbon before the emperor and left office, taking up a post with the Guangxi surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 巡行郡縣，土官有於元帥者，恃勢魚肉人，恐事覺，陰遣其子迓思誠於道。

translations.literal: Touring the prefectures and counties, a native official who had become a marshal relied on his power to oppress people; fearing exposure, he secretly sent his son to meet Sicheng on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On his tour of the prefectures and counties he found a native official who had become a marshal preying on the people. Fearful of exposure, the man secretly sent his son to greet Sicheng on the road.

sentences.zh: 思誠縛之，悉發其陰私，痛懲其罪，一道震肅。

translations.literal: Sicheng bound him, fully exposed his hidden crimes, and punished him severely; the whole circuit was shaken into order.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng had him bound, laid bare every hidden crime, and punished him severely; the whole circuit was shaken into discipline.

sentences.zh: 移浙西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇時為南台御史大夫，與江浙省臣有隙，嗾思誠劾之，思誠曰：「吾為天子耳目，不為台臣鷹犬也。」

translations.literal: Dashi Temur was then Grand Censor of the Southern Secretariat; he had a rift with the Zhejiang provincial officials and urged Sicheng to impeach them; Sicheng said, "I am the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears, not a hunting dog for the censorate officials."
translations.idiomatic: Dashi Temur was then southern regional censor-in-chief and at odds with the Zhejiang provincial ministers. He urged Sicheng to impeach them. Sicheng replied, "I serve as the emperor's eyes and ears, not as a censor's hunting dog."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 已而聞行省平章左吉貪墨，浙民多怨之，思誠奏疏其罪，流之海南。

translations.literal: Later he heard that Zuo Ji, Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat, was corrupt; the people of Zhe were much resentful; Sicheng memorialized detailing his crimes, and he was banished to Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he learned that Zuo Ji, grand councillor of the branch secretariat, was corrupt and widely hated in Zhejiang. Sicheng memorialized his crimes, and Zuo was exiled to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 復召為國子司業，遷中書左司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and promoted to Associate Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice chancellor of the Directorate of Education and promoted to associate director of the left secretariat.

sentences.zh: 盜殺河南省臣，以偽檄呼廉訪使段輔入行省事，及事敗，詿誤者三十餘人，將置於法，思誠言於朝，皆釋之。

translations.literal: Bandits killed a Henan provincial minister and used a forged dispatch to summon Surveillance Commissioner Duan Fu to enter and handle secretariat affairs; when the affair failed, more than thirty people who had been misled were about to be punished by law; Sicheng spoke to the court, and all were released.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits murdered a Henan provincial minister and used a forged order to summon surveillance commissioner Duan Fu to take charge of secretariat business. When the plot collapsed, more than thirty people caught up in the mistake were to be punished. Sicheng pleaded at court, and all were released.

sentences.zh: 升左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the left secretariat.

sentences.zh: 思誠素剛直，人多嫉之，遂以言罷。

translations.literal: Sicheng had always been upright and stern; many envied him, and he was dismissed on their word.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng had always been blunt and upright; many resented him, and he was removed on their complaints.

sentences.zh: 起為右司郎中，拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Director of the Right Secretariat and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed director of the right secretariat and made minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 科舉復行，與僉書樞密院事韓鏞為御試讀卷官。

translations.literal: When the civil examinations were restored, he and Associate Minister of the Privy Council Han Yong served as examiners for the imperial test.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil examinations were revived, he and Han Yong, associate minister of the privy council, served as imperial examiners.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，御史臺奏為治書侍御史，總裁遼、金、宋三史，升侍御史，樞密院奏為副使，御史臺留為侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites; the Censorate memorialized him as Associate Censor of the Secretariat; he supervised compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; he was promoted to Censor; the Privy Council memorialized him as Vice Minister, but the Censorate retained him as Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of rites, then was named associate censor by the Censorate, supervised compilation of the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, and was promoted to censor. The Privy Council wanted him as vice minister, but the Censorate kept him as censor.

sentences.zh: 會平章政事鞏卜班不法，監察御史劾之，御史大夫也先帖木兒曰：「姑徐之。」

translations.literal: When Grand Councillor Gongbu Ban acted unlawfully, the investigating censors impeached him; the Grand Censor Yesun Temur said, "Let it wait awhile."
translations.idiomatic: When grand councillor Gongbu Ban broke the law, investigating censors impeached him. Grand censor Yesun Temur said, "Let it wait a while."

sentences.zh: 思誠趣入奏，鞏卜班罷。

translations.literal: Sicheng hurried in to memorialize, and Gongbu Ban was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng rushed in to memorialize, and Gongbu Ban was removed.

sentences.zh: 大夫銜思誠，將謀擠之，思誠即謁告。

translations.literal: The Grand Censor harbored resentment toward Sicheng and was about to plot his removal; Sicheng immediately requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: The grand censor bore a grudge and was plotting to squeeze him out; Sicheng at once asked for leave.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知思誠無他，遷河東廉訪使。

translations.literal: The court knew Sicheng had no other designs and transferred him to Surveillance Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Sicheng had no ulterior motive and transferred him to Hedong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為集賢侍講學士，兼國子祭酒，出為湖廣行省參知政事，諸生抗疏留之，不可。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Academician Lecturer of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; he was sent out as Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat; the students submitted a joint memorial to keep him, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as lecturer in the Hall of Gathered Worthies and concurrent chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then sent out as vice administrator of the Huguang branch secretariat. Students petitioned to keep him, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 道中授湖北廉訪使，入拜中書參知政事，升左丞，轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: On the road he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Hubei; he entered court as Vice Administrator of the Central Secretariat, was promoted to Left Chancellor, and transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: En route he was named Hubei surveillance commissioner, then recalled as vice administrator of the central secretariat, promoted to left chancellor, and made vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 劾奏清道官不盡職，罷之。

translations.literal: He memorialized and impeached purification officers for not fulfilling their duties, and they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached purification officers who had neglected their duties, and they were removed.

sentences.zh: 再任左丞、知經筵事，提調國子監，兼翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史，加榮祿大夫，總裁后妃、功臣傳，會粹《六條政類》，帝賜玉帶，眷顧彌篤。

translations.literal: He again served as Left Chancellor and Director of Classics Lectures, supervised the Directorate of Education, and was concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Drafter of Edicts, and Compiler of the National History; he was given the honorary title Grand Master for Glorious Merit, supervised biographies of empresses and meritorious subjects, compiled the Six Categories of Government, received an imperial jade belt, and the emperor's favor grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as left chancellor and director of classics lectures, oversaw the Directorate of Education, and concurrently held the Hanlin academicianship, drafting of edicts, and national history compilation. He was given the honorary rank grand master for glorious merit, supervised biographies of empresses and meritorious subjects, compiled the Six Categories of Government, received an imperial jade belt, and won ever deeper favor.

sentences.zh: 又為樞密副使，仍知經筵事，復為中書左丞。

translations.literal: He again became Vice Minister of the Privy Council, still directed Classics Lectures, and again served as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again became privy council vice minister while continuing to direct classics lectures, and again served as left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫納麟，誣參政孔思立受賕事，或欲連中思誠，納麟曰：「呂左丞素有廉聲，難以及之。」

translations.literal: Grand Censor Nalin falsely charged Vice Administrator Kong Sili with taking bribes; some wished to implicate Sicheng as well; Nalin said, "Left Chancellor Lu has long had a reputation for integrity; it would be hard to reach him."
translations.idiomatic: Grand censor Nalin falsely accused vice administrator Kong Sili of bribery; some wanted to drag Sicheng into the case. Nalin said, "Left Chancellor Lu has long been known for integrity; he would be hard to touch."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 拜集賢學士，仍兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, still concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while remaining chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書契哲篤、左司都事武祺等，建言更鈔法，以楮幣一貫文省權銅錢一千文為母，銅錢為子，命廷臣集議。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Qie Zhedu, Director of Affairs of the Left Secretariat Wu Qi, and others proposed changing the paper-money law, making one string of paper notes in reduced denomination the mother and one thousand cash the child; the court ordered the ministers to assemble for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of personnel Qie Zhedu, left secretariat director Wu Qi, and others proposed revising the paper-money system so that one string of reduced-denomination notes would be the "mother" and a thousand cash the "child." The emperor ordered a full court discussion.

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「中統、至元自有母子，上料為母，下料為子，譬之蒙古人以漢人子為後，皆人類也，尚終為漢人之子，豈有故紙為父而立銅為子者乎？」

translations.literal: Sicheng said: "Zhongtong and Zhiyuan already have mother and child—upper denomination as mother, lower as child. It is like a Mongol taking a Han man's son as heir: both are human, yet in the end he is still a Han man's son. How could there be old paper as father and copper as son?"
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said, "Under Zhongtong and Zhiyuan the mother-child relation already exists—higher notes are mother, lower notes child. It is like a Mongol adopting a Han son: both are human, yet the child remains a Han son. Can old paper be made father and copper made son?"

sentences.zh: 一座咸笑。

translations.literal: The whole assembly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly laughed.

sentences.zh: 思誠又曰：「錢鈔用法，見為一致，以虛換實也。

translations.literal: Sicheng also said: "The use of cash and notes appears as one system, exchanging the insubstantial for the substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng went on, "Cash and notes are meant to work as one system, trading the insubstantial for the real.

sentences.zh: 今歷代錢、至正錢、中統鈔、至元鈔、交鈔分為五項，慮下民知之，藏其實而棄其虛，恐不利於國家也。」

translations.literal: Now the currencies of successive reigns, Zhiping cash, Zhongtong notes, Zhiyuan notes, and Jiaochao are divided into five items; I fear that if the common people learn this, they will hoard the real and discard the empty—perhaps not to the state's benefit."
translations.idiomatic: If we split successive coinages, Zhiping cash, Zhongtong notes, Zhiyuan notes, and Jiaochao into five kinds, the people will learn to hoard what is real and throw away what is empty. That may not help the state."

sentences.zh: 契哲篤曰：「至元鈔多偽，故更之爾。」

translations.literal: Qie Zhedu said: "Zhiyuan notes are largely counterfeit; that is why we change them."
translations.idiomatic: Qie Zhedu said, "Zhiyuan notes are mostly forged—that is why we are changing them."

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「至元鈔非偽，人為偽爾。

translations.literal: Sicheng said: "Zhiyuan notes are not counterfeit—men make them counterfeit.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng replied, "The Zhiyuan notes are not false; people make them false.

sentences.zh: 交鈔若出，亦為偽者矣。

translations.literal: If Jiaochao is issued, there will be forgers of it as well.
translations.idiomatic: If Jiaochao is issued, it will be forged too.

sentences.zh: 且至元鈔猶故戚也，家之童奴且識之；

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhiyuan notes are like an old in-law: even a household slave recognizes them;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zhiyuan notes are like an old in-law—even a servant boy knows them;

sentences.zh: 交鈔猶新戚也，雖不敢不親，人未識也，其偽反滋多爾。

translations.literal: Jiaochao is like a new in-law: though one dare not be distant, people do not yet know it, and counterfeits will only multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaochao is like a new in-law: you cannot snub him, yet no one knows him, and forgeries will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 況祖宗之成憲，其可輕改哉！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the settled statutes of the ancestors—can they be lightly altered?"
translations.idiomatic: And can the settled statutes of our ancestors be lightly changed?"

sentences.zh: 契哲篤曰：「祖宗法弊，亦可改矣。」

translations.literal: Qie Zhedu said: "When ancestral law is defective, it too may be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Qie Zhedu said, "When ancestral law is flawed, it may be changed."

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「汝輩更法，又欲上誣世皇，是汝與世皇爭高下也。

translations.literal: Sicheng said: "You people change the law and also wish to slander Emperor Shizu above—this is you contending with Emperor Shizu for superiority.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said, "You change the law and then want to blame Emperor Shizu from above—that is you competing with Emperor Shizu for stature.

sentences.zh: 且自世皇以來，諸帝皆諡曰孝，改其成憲，可謂孝乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, since Emperor Shizu, every emperor has been given the posthumous title "Filial"; to alter his settled statutes—can that be called filial?"
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Shizu every emperor has been given the posthumous title Filial. To alter his settled statutes—is that filial?"

sentences.zh: 契哲篤曰：「錢鈔兼行何如？」

translations.literal: Qie Zhedu said: "What if cash and notes circulate together?"
translations.idiomatic: Qie Zhedu asked, "What if cash and notes circulated together?"

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「錢鈔兼行，輕重不倫，何者為母，何者為子？

translations.literal: Sicheng said: "If cash and notes circulate together, light and heavy are not in proportion—which is mother, which is child?
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said, "If cash and notes circulate together, their weight and value will not match—which is mother, which child?

sentences.zh: 汝不通古今，道聽而途說，何足行哉！」

translations.literal: You do not understand past and present; you hear things on the road and repeat them—how could that be carried out?"
translations.idiomatic: You know neither past nor present; you pick up gossip on the road—how can that be enacted?"

sentences.zh: 契哲篤忿曰：「我等策既不可行，公有何策？」

translations.literal: Qie Zhedu said angrily: "Since our plan cannot be carried out, what plan do you, sir, have?"
translations.idiomatic: Qie Zhedu snapped, "If our plan will not work, what is yours, sir?"

sentences.zh: 思誠曰：「我有三字策曰：行不得！

translations.literal: Sicheng said: "I have a three-character plan: It cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng said, "I have a three-word plan: It cannot be done!

sentences.zh: 行不得！」

translations.literal: It cannot be done!"
translations.idiomatic: It cannot be done!"

sentences.zh: 丞相脫脫見思誠言直，頗狐疑未決。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Toghto, seeing Sicheng's words were blunt, was rather doubtful and undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councillor Toghto, hearing how blunt Sicheng was, wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫也先帖木兒獨曰：「呂祭酒之言亦有是者，但不當在廟堂上大聲歷色爾。」

translations.literal: Grand Censor Yesun Temur alone said: "Academician Lu's words also have something to them, but he ought not to have raised his voice and changed color in the ancestral hall."
translations.idiomatic: Grand censor Yesun Temur alone said, "Academician Lu is not entirely wrong, but he should not have shouted and flushed in the imperial hall."

sentences.zh: 已而監察御史承望風旨，劾思誠狂妄，奪其誥命並所賜玉帶，复左遷湖廣行省左丞，遣太醫院宣使秦初即其家迫遣之。

translations.literal: Soon investigating censors, courting the prevailing wind, impeached Sicheng for arrogance; his patent of appointment and the jade belt he had been given were both taken away; he was again demoted to Left Chancellor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat; the Imperial Medical Academy dispatched Commissioner Qin Chu to his home to hurry him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Soon investigating censors, reading the wind, impeached him for arrogance. His patent and jade belt were stripped, and he was again demoted to left chancellor of the Huguang branch secretariat. The Imperial Medical Academy sent commissioner Qin Chu to his house to hurry him away.

sentences.zh: 初窘辱之，不遺餘力，思誠不為動。

translations.literal: At first Qin humiliated him without sparing any effort; Sicheng was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qin humiliated him with all his might; Sicheng did not stir.

sentences.zh: 貽書參議龔伯遂曰：「去年許可用為河南左丞，今年呂思誠為湖廣左丞，世事至此，足下得無動心乎？」

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Secretariat Councillor Gong Bosui saying: "Last year Xu Keyong was made Left Chancellor of Henan; this year Lu Sicheng is made Left Chancellor of Huguang—affairs have come to this; can you, sir, remain unmoved?"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to secretariat councillor Gong Bosui: "Last year Xu Keyong was made left chancellor of Henan; this year Lu Sicheng is made left chancellor of Huguang. When things have come to this, can you, sir, stay unmoved?"

sentences.zh: 抵武昌城下，語諸將曰：「賊據城與諸君相持經久，必不知吾為此來，出其不意，可以入城。」

translations.literal: When he reached below the walls of Wuchang, he told the generals: "The bandits hold the city and have been at stalemate with you for a long time; they surely do not know I have come for this; take them by surprise and you can enter the city."
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Wuchang, he told the generals, "The rebels have held the city against you for a long time. They cannot know I have come. Take them by surprise and you can enter."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He set out at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將不獲已，隨其後，竟不煩轉鬥而入。

translations.literal: The generals had no choice but to follow behind him; in the end they entered without needing to turn and fight.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had no choice but to follow. They entered the city without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 詢其故，賊倉卒無備。

translations.literal: When he inquired the reason, the bandits had been caught unprepared in their haste.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, they learned the rebels had been caught utterly unprepared.

sentences.zh: 盡驚走。

translations.literal: All fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: They fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 思誠乃大會軍民官吏告之曰：「賊去，示吾弱也，規將復來。」

translations.literal: Sicheng then assembled the army, the people, and officials and told them: "The bandits have gone—this shows our weakness; they intend to return."
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng then gathered soldiers, civilians, and officials and said, "The rebels have left—that shows our weakness. They mean to come back."

sentences.zh: 於是申號令，戒職事，修器械，葺城郭，明部伍，先謀自守，徐議出征。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued orders, warned those on duty, repaired weapons, mended the walls, clarified unit organization, first planned self-defense, and only then slowly discussed taking the field.
translations.idiomatic: He reissued commands, tightened discipline, repaired arms, rebuilt the walls, sorted the ranks, secured the defenses first, and only then talked of marching out.

sentences.zh: 苗軍暴橫，侵辱省憲，思誠正色叱之曰：「若等能殺呂左丞乎？」

translations.literal: Miao troops were violent and overbearing, insulting the provincial and surveillance officials; Sicheng sternly rebuked them: "Can you kill Left Chancellor Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Miao troops were brutal and insulted the provincial and surveillance officers. Sicheng rebuked them coldly: "Can you kill Left Chancellor Lu?"

sentences.zh: 自是無敢復至。

translations.literal: From then on none dared come again.
translations.idiomatic: After that none dared approach again.

sentences.zh: 曾未數日，召還，復為中書左丞。

translations.literal: Before many days had passed he was recalled and again made Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was recalled and again made left chancellor of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 思誠去二日，城復陷。

translations.literal: Two days after Sicheng left, the city again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Sicheng left, the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 移光祿大夫、大司農。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as grand master of splendid happiness and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄得疾，以至正十七年三月十七日卒，年六十有五。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he fell ill, and on the seventeenth day of the third month of the seventeenth year of Zhizheng he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took ill and died on the seventeenth day of the third month of Zhizheng 17, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 思誠氣宇凝定，素以勁拔聞，不為勢利所屈。

translations.literal: Sicheng's bearing was composed and steadfast; he had long been known for vigorous integrity and would not bow to power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng bore himself with composed steadiness, was renowned for resolute integrity, and would not yield to power or gain.

sentences.zh: 三為祭酒，一法許衡之舊，諸生從化，後多為名士。

translations.literal: Three times he served as Libationer, following Xu Heng's former practices in one unified method; the students were transformed by his teaching, and many later became noted scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice he served as libationer, adhering consistently to Xu Heng's earlier methods; his students were swayed by his example, and many later rose to distinction.

sentences.zh: 嘗病古注疏太繁，魏了翁刪之太簡，將約其中以成書，不果。

translations.literal: He once deplored that the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries were too prolix, while Wei Liaoweng had abridged them too severely; he intended to strike a middle course and complete a book, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He once lamented that ancient commentaries were too dense and that Wei Liaoweng's abridgment was too spare; he planned to reconcile the two in a single work but never finished it.

sentences.zh: 有文集若干卷、《兩漢通紀》若干卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection of writings of several fascicles and a General Chronicle of the Two Han of several fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His literary remains comprise several fascicles of collected works and several fascicles of A General Chronicle of the Two Han.

sentences.zh: 諡忠肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: ○汪澤民

translations.literal: ○ Wang Zemin
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zemin

sentences.zh: 汪澤民，字叔志，徽之婺源州人，宋端明殿學士藻之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Zemin, courtesy name Shuzhi, was a native of Wuyuan Prefecture in Huizhou, seventh-generation descendant of the Song Duanming Hall Academician Wang Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zemin (Shuzhi), a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou, was the seventh-generation descendant of the Song academician Wang Zao of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 少警悟，家貧力學，既長，遂通諸經。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive; though his family was poor he studied with tireless effort, and once grown he mastered all the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and keen from boyhood, he studied hard despite poverty; in adulthood he had mastered the full canon of classics.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，以《春秋》中鄉貢，上禮部，下第，授寧國路儒學正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou reign he passed the provincial examination in the Spring and Autumn Annals, went up to the Ministry of Rites, failed the metropolitan examination, and was appointed Instructor at the Confucian school of Ningguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanyou he qualified in the provincial examinations on the Annals, then failed at the Ministry of Rites; he was appointed Confucian instructor in Ningguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，遂登進士第，授承事郎、同知岳州路平江州事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he attained the jinshi degree and was appointed Gentleman for Affairs and Vice Commissioner of the administrative affairs of Pingjiang Prefecture under Yuezhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he passed the jinshi examinations and was made gentleman for affairs and vice prefect of Pingjiang under Yuezhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以母年八十，上書願奪所授官一等或二等，得近地以便養，不允。

translations.literal: Because his mother was eighty, he submitted a memorial asking to be reduced one or two ranks from the office just granted so that he might receive a nearby post to support her; this was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being eighty, he petitioned to be demoted one or two ranks in exchange for a nearby post to care for her; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 南歸奉母之官。

translations.literal: He returned south and took her with him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He returned south and brought his mother to his office.

sentences.zh: 州民李氏，以貲雄，其弟死，妻誓不他適，兄利其財，嗾族人誣婦以姦事。

translations.literal: A commoner of the prefecture surnamed Li, wealthy and overbearing, had a younger brother who died; the wife vowed not to marry another, but the elder brother coveted her property and incited clansmen to accuse the widow of adultery.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy townsman surnamed Li had a brother who died; the widow swore she would not remarry, but the elder brother coveted her estate and goaded kinsmen to accuse her of adultery.

sentences.zh: 獄成而澤民至，察知其枉，為直之。

translations.literal: The case had been concluded when Zemin arrived; perceiving the injustice, he set the matter right.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the case was closed and Zemin arrived, he saw the injustice and reversed the verdict.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷徵江南包銀，府檄澤民分辨，民不擾而事​​集。

translations.literal: Just then the court levied the bao-yin silver tax in Jiangnan; the prefecture ordered Zemin to apportion it, and the people were not disturbed while the task was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court imposed the bao-yin levy on Jiangnan, the prefecture put Zemin in charge of apportioning it; the people were not troubled and the collection was completed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南安路總管府推官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Nan'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to reviewing official in the Nan'an chief administrator's office.

sentences.zh: 鎮守萬戶朵兒赤，持官府短長，郡吏王甲，毆傷屬縣長官，訴郡，同僚畏朵兒赤，托故不視事，澤民獨捕甲，系之獄。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Wanhu Dorbet, who knew the failings of the government offices, had a prefectural clerk Wang Jia who beat and injured a magistrate of a subordinate county; the case was brought to the prefecture, but colleagues feared Dorbet and excused themselves from hearing it; Zemin alone arrested Jia and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Dorbet knew every weakness in the local administration. When a prefectural clerk named Wang Jia assaulted a county magistrate, colleagues feared Dorbet and declined the case; Zemin alone arrested Wang Jia and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 朵兒赤賂巡按御史，受甲家人訴，欲出之，澤民正色與辨，御史沮怍，夜竟去，乃卒罪王甲。

translations.literal: Dorbet bribed the touring surveillance censor, who accepted the petition from Jia's family and wished to release him; Zemin spoke sternly in argument, the censor was shamed and abashed and fled in the night, and Jia was finally punished.
translations.idiomatic: Dorbet bribed the touring censor, who took the family's petition and tried to free Jia. Zemin argued him down face to face; the censor withdrew in shame that night, and Wang Jia was convicted at last.

sentences.zh: 潮州府判官錢珍，以姦淫事殺推官梁楫，事連廣東廉訪副使劉珍，坐系者二百餘人，省府官凡六委官鞫問，皆顧忌淹延弗能白，复檄澤民讞之，獄立具，人服其明。

translations.literal: Qian Zhen, prefectural judge of Chaozhou, had killed the reviewing official Liang Ji over an affair of debauchery; the case implicated Liu Zhen, deputy surveillance commissioner of Guangdong; more than two hundred persons were detained; six times provincial and circuit officials commissioned officers to interrogate, but all hesitated and delayed and could not clear the matter; again they ordered Zemin to report on the case, and the dossier was immediately complete—men admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou's prefectural judge Qian Zhen murdered reviewing official Liang Ji in a scandal of adultery that implicated Guangdong's deputy surveillance commissioner Liu Zhen. More than two hundred people were held; six rounds of officials sent to investigate shrank back from the powerful interests involved. When Zemin was ordered to try the case, he concluded it at once, and all marveled at his discernment.

sentences.zh: 遷信州路總管府推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Xinzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to reviewing official in the Xinzhou chief administrator's office.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，授平江路總管府推官。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Reviewing Official in the Chief Administrator's office of Pingjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he was appointed reviewing official in the Pingjiang chief administrator's office.

sentences.zh: 有僧淨廣，與他僧有憾，久絕往來，一日，邀廣飲，廣弟子急欲得師財，且苦其棰楚，潛往它僧所殺之。

translations.literal: There was a monk Jingguang who bore a grudge against another monk and had long ceased visiting him; one day he invited Guang to drink; Guang's disciple, eager to seize his master's property and weary of his beatings, secretly went to the other monk's place and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Jingguang had a feud with another monk and had long ceased visiting him. One day he invited Guang to drink. Guang's disciple, eager for his master's property and weary of his beatings, stole to the rival monk's quarters and killed him.

sentences.zh: 明日訴官，它僧不勝考掠，乃誣服，三經審錄，詞無異，結案等報。

translations.literal: The next day the case was reported to the authorities; the other monk could not endure the torture and falsely confessed; through three rounds of examination the testimony did not change, and the case was closed awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the crime was reported. The other monk broke under torture and confessed falsely. After three examinations his story never changed, and the case was closed pending execution.

sentences.zh: 澤民取行凶刀視之，刀上有鐵工姓名，召工問之，乃其弟子刀也，一訊吐實，即械之而出他僧，人驚以為神。

translations.literal: Zemin examined the murder weapon and found on the blade the name of the ironsmith; he summoned the smith and learned it was the disciple's knife; on one interrogation the truth came out, and he immediately shackled the disciple and released the other monk—people were astonished and called it divine.
translations.idiomatic: Zemin inspected the murder weapon and found an ironsmith's mark on the blade. The smith identified it as the disciple's knife. One interrogation brought out the truth; Zemin shackled the disciple and freed the other monk, and people called it uncanny.

sentences.zh: 調濟寧路兗州知州，孔子後衍聖公襲封職三品，澤民建議，以謂宜升其品秩，以示褒崇宣聖之意，廷議從之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit; the Yanshenggong, lineal descendant of Confucius, held a third-rank hereditary enfeoffment; Zemin proposed that his rank should be raised to show honor to the Sage, and the court deliberation approved.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to prefect of Yanzhou in Jining Circuit, he proposed raising the hereditary third-rank title of Confucius's descendant the Yanshenggong to show the court's reverence for the Sage; the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 至正三年，朝廷修遼、金、宋史，召澤民赴闕，除國子司業，與修史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng the court undertook to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Zemin was summoned to the capital, appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and took part in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 3, when the court set about compiling the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song, Zemin was summoned to court, made vice director of the directorate of education, and joined the editorial staff.

sentences.zh: 書成，遷集賢直學士，階太中大夫。

translations.literal: When the work was completed he was promoted to Academician-in-Attendance of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were finished he was promoted to academician-in-attendance of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, with the rank of grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 未兩月，即移書告老。

translations.literal: Before two months had passed he submitted a letter requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Less than two months later he submitted his resignation.

sentences.zh: 大學士和尚曰：「集賢、翰林，實養老尊賢之地，先生何為遽去？

translations.literal: The grand academician Heshang said: "The Hall of Gathered Worthies and the Hanlin Academy are truly places to honor the aged and esteem the worthy—why does the Master hurry away?
translations.idiomatic: Grand academician Heshang said, "The Hall of Gathered Worthies and the Hanlin Academy are meant to honor the aged and esteem the worthy—why leave so soon?

sentences.zh: 願少留，以副上意。」

translations.literal: I beg you to remain a little longer to fulfill the Emperor's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Stay a little longer to satisfy the throne's wish."

sentences.zh: 澤民曰：「以布衣叨榮三品，志願足矣。」

translations.literal: Zemin said: "As a commoner I have been favored with the glory of the third rank; my wish is fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Zemin replied, "A plain scholar raised to the third rank—my wish is fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 遂以嘉議大夫、禮部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he retired with the rank of Grand Master for Exalted Counsel and as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired with the rank of grand master for exalted counsel and as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 既歸田裡，與門生故人相往返嬉遊，超然若忘世者。

translations.literal: Once he had returned to his fields, he went back and forth with students and old friends in leisurely visits, detached as though he had forgotten the world.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his home district he visited and roamed with students and old friends, aloof as if the world no longer concerned him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，蘄黃賊陷徽州，時澤民居宣州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Qihuang rebels seized Huizhou; at that time Zemin was living in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Qihuang rebels took Huizhou; Zemin was then living in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而賊來犯宣州，江東廉訪使道童雅重澤民，日就之詢守禦計，城得無虞。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels came to attack Xuanzhou; the Jiangdong surveillance commissioner Daotong, who greatly valued Zemin, came daily to consult him on plans for defense, and the city remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels attacked Xuanzhou. Surveillance commissioner Daotong of Jiangdong, who held Zemin in high regard, consulted him daily on defense, and the city was preserved.

sentences.zh: 明年，長槍軍瑣南班等叛，來寇城，或勸澤民去，澤民曰：「我雖無官守，故受國厚恩，臨危愛死，非臣子節。」

translations.literal: The next year the Changqiang Army under Suonanban and others rebelled and came to assault the city; some urged Zemin to flee; Zemin said: "Though I hold no office, I have long received the state's deep favor; to cling to life in peril is not the conduct of a loyal subject."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Suonanban and others of the Changqiang Army rebelled and besieged the city. Some urged Zemin to flee. He said, "I hold no office, yet the state has shown me great favor. To flee in danger is not the way of a loyal subject."

sentences.zh: 留不去，凡戰鬥籌畫，多澤民參決之，累敗賊兵。

translations.literal: He remained and did not leave; in planning for battle he took part in many decisions, and repeatedly defeated the rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed. In battle and strategy he took part in many decisions and repeatedly defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 既而寇益眾，城陷，澤民為所執。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits grew more numerous and the city fell; Zemin was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy grew in strength, the city fell, and Zemin was captured.

sentences.zh: 使之降，大罵不屈，遂遇害，年七十。

translations.literal: They ordered him to submit; he cursed them loudly and would not yield, and was thereupon killed, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded his surrender; he cursed them and refused to yield, and was killed at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈資善大夫、江浙行中書省左丞，追封譙國郡公，諡文節。

translations.literal: When word reached the court he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Assisting Goodness and Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao with retroactive title, and given the posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: On report the court posthumously made him grand master for assisting goodness and left chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qiao, and gave him the posthumous title Cultivated Integrity.

sentences.zh: ○幹文傳

translations.literal: ○ Gan Wenchuan
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenchuan

sentences.zh: 幹文傳，字壽道，平江人。

translations.literal: Gan Wenchuan, courtesy name Shoudao, was a native of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenchuan (Shoudao) was a native of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 祖宗顯，宋承信郎。

translations.literal: His ancestor Xian had been a Gentleman for Trust under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Xian had been a Song gentleman for trust.

sentences.zh: 父雷龍，鄉貢進士。

translations.literal: His father Leilong was a provincial graduate who passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Leilong had passed the provincial and jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 宗顯之先世以武弁入官，而力教其子以文易武，故雷龍兩舉進士，宋亡，不及仕。

translations.literal: Xian's forebears had entered office as military officers, yet he strove to teach his son to replace arms with letters; thus Leilong twice passed the jinshi examination, but the Song fell before he could take office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's family had entered service as military officers, but he pressed his son to trade the sword for the brush. Leilong twice passed the jinshi examinations, yet the Song fell before he could serve.

sentences.zh: 及生文傳，乃名今名以期之。

translations.literal: When Wenchuan was born they gave him a given name that expressed this hope.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenchuan was born they chose a given name that expressed this hope.

sentences.zh: 文傳少嗜學，十歲能屬文，未冠，已有聲譽，用舉者為吳及金壇兩縣學教諭、饒州慈湖書院山長。

translations.literal: Wenchuan from youth loved learning; at ten he could compose prose, and before he came of age he already had a reputation; through recommendation he served as Instructor in the schools of Wu and Jintan counties and as Head of the Cihu Academy in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Wenchuan loved learning. At ten he could write prose, and before his capping he was already known. By recommendation he taught in the schools of Wu and Jintan and headed the Cihu Academy in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 仁守詔舉進士，文傳首登延祐二年乙科，授同知昌國州事，累遷長洲、烏程兩縣尹，升婺源知州，又知吳江州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ordered the jinshi examination, Wenchuan was first in the second class of the second year of Yanyou, appointed Vice Commissioner of the affairs of Changguo Prefecture, successively promoted to Magistrate of Changzhou and Wucheng counties, then Prefect of Wuyuan, and then of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ordered the jinshi examination, Wenchuan topped the second class in Yanyou 2, became vice commissioner at Changguo, rose to magistrate of Changzhou and Wucheng, then prefect of Wuyuan and Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 文傳長於治劇，所至俱有善政。

translations.literal: Wenchuan excelled at handling urgent affairs; wherever he went he left good government.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchuan excelled at urgent administration; everywhere he served he left sound government.

sentences.zh: 自其始至昌國，即能柔之以恩信，於是海島之民，雖頑獷不易治，至有剽掠海中若化外然者，亦為之變俗。

translations.literal: From his first posting at Changguo he was able to soften the people with kindness and trust; thus the island folk, though stubborn and hard to govern and even given to plunder on the sea as though beyond the pale, also changed their ways.
translations.idiomatic: From his first posting at Changguo he won the people with kindness and trust. Even the islanders—stubborn, unruly, and given to raiding the seas as if beyond the empire—changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 初，長官強愎自恣，文傳推誠以待之，久乃自屈服。

translations.literal: At first the chief official was overbearing and willful; Wenchuan treated him with sincere openness, and in time he yielded of himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first the chief official was arrogant and self-willed. Wenchuan met him with sincere openness until in time he submitted of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 鹽場官方倚轉運司勢，虐使州民，家業破盪，文傳語同列曰：「吾屬受天子命，以牧此民，可坐視而弗之救乎！」

translations.literal: The salt-yard officials, relying on the power of the transport commission, cruelly pressed the people of the prefecture until families were ruined; Wenchuan said to his colleagues: "We have received the Son of Heaven's commission to shepherd these people—can we sit by and not save them?"
translations.idiomatic: Salt-yard officials, backed by the transport commission, abused the prefectural people until households were ruined. Wenchuan told his colleagues, "We hold the Son of Heaven's commission to shepherd these people—can we sit by and not save them?"

sentences.zh: 乃亟為陳理，上官莫能奪，民賴以免。

translations.literal: He thereupon urgently laid out the case, and the superior could not overrule him; the people were spared.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the case at once. His superiors could not overrule him, and the people were spared.

sentences.zh: 長洲為文傳鄉邑，文傳徙榻公署，無事未嘗輒出，而親舊莫敢通私謁。

translations.literal: Changzhou was Wenchuan's home district; he moved his couch to the public office and on ordinary days never went out, and neither kin nor friends dared pay private calls.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou was Wenchuan's home district. He kept his couch in the yamen and rarely left on ordinary business; kin and friends did not dare pay private calls.

sentences.zh: 會創行助役法，凡民田百畝，令以三畝入官，為受役者之助。

translations.literal: Just then the corvée-assistance law was introduced: for every hundred mu of civilian land, three mu were to be turned over to the government as aid for those bearing corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: The corvée-assistance law was then introduced: for every hundred mu of civilian land, three mu were turned over to the state to support those bearing corvée duty.

sentences.zh: 文傳既專任其縣事，而行省又以無錫州及華亭、上海兩縣之事諉焉。

translations.literal: Wenchuan had sole charge of his county's affairs, and the branch secretariat also entrusted him with the affairs of Wuxi Prefecture and the counties of Huating and Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchuan had sole charge of his county, and the branch secretariat also entrusted him with Wuxi prefecture and the counties of Huating and Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 文傳諭豪家大姓，以腴田來歸，而中人之家，自是不病於役。

translations.literal: Wenchuan persuaded the great clans to surrender their fertile fields, and thereafter middle households were no longer crushed by corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded great clans to surrender fertile fields, and middle households were no longer ruined by corvée.

sentences.zh: 其在烏程，有富民張甲之妻王，無子，張納一妾於外，生子，未晬，王誘妾以兒來，尋逐妾，殺兒焚之。

translations.literal: While he was in Wucheng, a wealthy man Zhang Jia's wife Wang had no son; Zhang took a concubine outside the home who bore a son; before the child was weaned, Wang lured the concubine to bring the boy in, then drove the concubine away, killed the child, and burned the body.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng, a rich man Zhang Jia's wife Wang was childless. Zhang took an outside concubine who bore a son. Before the infant was weaned, Wang lured the concubine to bring the boy in, then drove her off, killed the child, and burned the body.

sentences.zh: 文傳聞而發其事，得死兒餘骨，王厚賄妾之父母，買鄰家兒為妾所生，兒初不死。

translations.literal: When Wenchuan heard of it he uncovered the affair, recovered the child's remaining bones, and Wang heavily bribed the concubine's parents to buy a neighbor's child and claim he was the concubine's son and had not died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchuan uncovered the crime and recovered the child's bones. Wang bribed the concubine's parents to buy a neighbor's child and claim the infant had not died.

sentences.zh: 文傳令妾抱兒乳之，兒啼不就乳，妾之父母吐實，乃呼鄰婦至，兒見之，躍入其懷，乳之即飲，王遂伏辜。

translations.literal: Wenchuan ordered the concubine to hold the child and nurse him; the child cried and would not take the breast; the concubine's parents confessed the truth; he then summoned the neighbor's wife—the child at sight leaped into her arms and drank at once when she nursed him—and Wang was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He had the concubine nurse the child; the infant cried and refused her breast. Her parents confessed. He summoned the neighbor's wife—the child leaped into her arms and nursed at once—and Wang was punished.

sentences.zh: 丹徒縣民有二弟共殺其姊者，獄久不決，浙西廉訪司俾文傳鞫之，既得其情，其母乞貸二子命，為終養計，文傳謂二人所承有輕重，以首從論，則為首者當死，司官從之。

translations.literal: In Dantu County two younger brothers together had killed their elder sister; the case long went unresolved; the Jiangxi surveillance commission ordered Wenchuan to try it; once he had the facts, their mother begged to spare both sons' lives for her final support; Wenchuan said the degrees of guilt differed—by the law of principal and accessory the leader must die—and the commission officer agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dantu two younger brothers had killed their elder sister; the case dragged on. Jiangxi surveillance sent Wenchuan to try it. When he had the facts, their mother begged to spare both for her old age. Wenchuan held that guilt differed—by principal and accessory law the leader must die—and the officer agreed.

sentences.zh: 婺源之俗，男女婚聘後，富則渝其約，有育其女至老死不嫁者；

translations.literal: The custom of Wuyuan was that after betrothal, if the man grew rich he broke the engagement, and some reared their daughters until old age without marrying them;
translations.idiomatic: In Wuyuan, after betrothal a man who grew rich might break the match; some reared daughters until old age unmarried;

sentences.zh: 親喪，貧則不舉，有停其柩累數世不葬者。

translations.literal: when kin died, if the family was poor they did not conduct the funeral, and some kept the coffin for many generations without burial.
translations.idiomatic: when kin died the poor might not bury them, and some kept coffins unburied for generations.

sentences.zh: 文傳下車，即召其耆老，使以禮訓告之，閱三月而婚喪俱畢。

translations.literal: When Wenchuan took office he at once summoned the elders and had them instruct the people in ritual; within three months weddings and funerals were all completed.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he summoned the elders to instruct the people in ritual; within three months weddings and funerals were settled.

sentences.zh: 宋大儒硃熹，上世居婺源，故業為豪民所佔，子孫訴於有司，莫能直，文傳諭其民以理，不煩窮治而悉歸之。

translations.literal: The great Song scholar Zhu Xi's forebears had lived in Wuyuan; their estate had been seized by powerful families, and the descendants sued at the yamen but could not obtain justice; Wenchuan instructed the people in reason, and without exhaustive prosecution all was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi's ancestors had lived in Wuyuan; powerful families had seized their estate, and descendants' suits failed. Wenchuan persuaded the people by reason, and without harsh prosecution all was restored.

sentences.zh: 复募好義者，即其故宅基建祠，俾硃氏世守焉。

translations.literal: He again recruited men of good will to build a shrine on the old homestead and had the Zhu clan guard it in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited men of goodwill to build a shrine on the old homestead for the Zhu clan to guard in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 有富民江丙，出遊京師，娶娼女張為婦，江既客死，張走數千里，返其柩以葬，前妻之子因苦之，既而殺之，瘞其屍山谷間。

translations.literal: A wealthy man Jiang Bing went to the capital on business and married a courtesan Zhang as his wife; Jiang died abroad, and Zhang traveled thousands of li to return his coffin for burial; the son by his first wife tormented her and then killed her, burying the corpse in a mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: A rich man Jiang Bing went to the capital and married the courtesan Zhang. He died abroad; Zhang traveled thousands of li to bring his coffin home. His son by the first wife harassed her, then killed her and buried her in a mountain valley.

sentences.zh: 官司知之，利其賄不問，文傳乃發其事，而論如法。

translations.literal: The authorities knew of it but, profiting from bribes, did not inquire; Wenchuan uncovered the affair and sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials knew but took bribes and did nothing; Wenchuan uncovered the crime and punished by law.

sentences.zh: 文傳蒞官，其所設施多此類，故其治行往往為諸州縣最。

translations.literal: In his offices Wenchuan enacted many measures of this kind; thus his administrative record was often the foremost among prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: His administrations were full of such cases; his record was often the best in the circuit.

sentences.zh: 韓鏞時僉浙西廉訪司事，作《烏程謠》以紀其績，論者謂其有古循吏之風。

translations.literal: When Han Yong was commissioner of the Jiangxi surveillance commission he composed the "Ballad of Wucheng" to record his achievements; critics said he had the manner of the ancient compassionate officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yong served on the Jiangxi surveillance commission he wrote the "Ballad of Wucheng" to record his deeds; critics said he had the air of the ancient compassionate magistrates.

sentences.zh: 至正三年，召赴闕，承詔預修《宋史》，書成，賞賚優渥，仍有旨四品以下各進一官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng he was summoned to court, received the edict to take part in compiling the History of Song; when the work was completed the rewards were generous, and there was also an order that all below the fourth rank should advance one step in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 3 he was summoned to court to help compile the History of Song. When it was finished the rewards were generous, and all officials below the fourth rank were advanced one step.

sentences.zh: 擢文傳集賢待制。

translations.literal: Wenchuan was promoted to Academician-in-Waiting of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchuan was promoted to academician-in-waiting of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 亡何，以嘉議大夫、禮部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired with the rank of Grand Master for Exalted Counsel and as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired as grand master for exalted counsel and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 文傳氣貌充偉，識度凝遠，喜接引後進，考試江浙、江西鄉闈，所取士後多知名。

translations.literal: Wenchuan's bearing was full and imposing, his judgment composed and far-reaching; he delighted in guiding younger scholars; in examining the provincial examinations of Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Jiangxi, many of those he selected later became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchuan was imposing in presence, composed and far-sighted in judgment, and delighted in guiding younger scholars. In the Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Jiangxi provincial examinations many he chose later rose to fame.

sentences.zh: 為文務雅正，不事浮藻，其於政事為尤長云。

translations.literal: In writing he strove for elegance and correctness and did not pursue florid ornament; in government he was especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: His writing aimed at elegance and correctness, not ornament; in government he was especially accomplished.

sentences.zh: ○韓鏞

translations.literal: ○ Han Yong
translations.idiomatic: Han Yong

sentences.zh: 韓鏞，字伯高，濟南人。

translations.literal: Han Yong, courtesy name Bogao, was a native of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yong (Bogao) was a native of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年中進士第，授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，尋遷集賢都事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Gentleman for Service and Compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute; soon he was promoted to Director of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 5 he passed the jinshi examinations, became gentleman for service and compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute, and soon rose to director of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，轉國子博士，俄拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he was transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education; soon he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 4 he became erudite of the directorate of education, then investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 當時由進士入官者僅百之一，由吏致位顯要者常十之九。

translations.literal: At that time only about one in a hundred who entered office came through the jinshi, while those who rose to prominence through clerical service were commonly nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: At the time only about one in a hundred officials had entered by the jinshi route, while nine in ten who reached high office had risen from clerical posts.

sentences.zh: 帝乃欲以中書參議傅巖起為吏部尚書，鏞上言：「吏部掌天下銓衡，岩起從吏入官，烏足盡知天下賢才。

translations.literal: The Emperor then wished to appoint the Central Secretariat Counselor Fu Yanqi Minister of Personnel; Yong memorialized: "The Ministry of Personnel holds the scales of appointment for the empire; Yanqi entered office through clerical service—how can he fully know the empire's worthy talents?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make central secretariat counselor Fu Yanqi minister of personnel. Yong memorialized, "Personnel holds the empire's scales of appointment. Yanqi came up through clerical service—how can he know all the empire's worthy men?

sentences.zh: 況尚書秩三品，岩起累官四品耳，於法亦不得升。」

translations.literal: Moreover the Minister's rank is third grade, while Yanqi's accumulated offices are only fourth grade—in law he also may not be promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the minister is third rank while Yanqi has only reached fourth—in law he cannot be promoted."

sentences.zh: 制可其奏。

translations.literal: The edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，除僉浙西廉訪司事，擊姦暴，黜貪墨，而特舉烏程縣尹幹文傳治行為諸縣最，所至郡縣，為之肅然。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansli he was appointed Commissioner of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission; he struck down the wicked and violent and dismissed the greedy and corrupt, and especially commended Wucheng Magistrate Gan Wenchuan, whose administration was foremost among counties; wherever he went, prefectures and counties were brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansli 1 he became commissioner of the Jiangxi surveillance commission, struck down the violent and dismissed the corrupt, and especially commended Wucheng magistrate Gan Wenchuan as the best in the circuit; wherever he went, prefectures and counties were brought to order.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉江浙財賦副總管。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Deputy Chief Controller of Jiangsu-Zhejiang Finance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became deputy chief controller of Jiangsu-Zhejiang finance.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，除國子司業，尋遷南行台治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; soon he was promoted to Investigating Attendant Censor of the Southern Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 he became vice director of the directorate of education, then investigating attendant censor of the southern censorate.

sentences.zh: 順帝初，歷僉宣徽及樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shundi's reign he successively served as Commissioner of the Bureau of Imperial Manufactories and of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Shundi's accession he served in turn as commissioner of the bureau of imperial manufactories and of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，除翰林侍講學士，既而拜侍御史，以剛介為時所忌，言事者誣劾其贓私，乃罷去。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was appointed Hanlin Attendant Academic Lecturer; soon he was made Attendant Censor; because of his stern integrity he was envied by his time; those who spoke in court falsely impeached him for corruption and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 2 he became Hanlin attendant academic lecturer, then attendant censor. His stern integrity made him envied; court speakers falsely impeached him for graft and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五年，台臣辨其誣，遂復起參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the censorate cleared the false charge and he was again raised to Counselor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 5 the censorate cleared the slander and he was restored as counselor of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，朝廷慎選​​守令，參知政事魏中立言於帝：「當今必欲得賢守令，無加鏞者。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as the court carefully chose prefects and magistrates, Counselor Wei Zhongli said to the Emperor: "If we must have worthy prefects and magistrates today, none surpass Yong."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as the court carefully chose prefects and magistrates, counselor Wei Zhongli told the emperor, "If we want worthy prefects and magistrates today, none surpass Yong."

sentences.zh: 帝乃特署鏞姓名，授饒州路總管。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon specially wrote Yong's name and appointed him Chief Administrator of Raozhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote Yong's name and appointed him chief administrator of Raozhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 饒之為俗尚鬼，有覺山廟者，自昔為妖以禍福人，為盜賊者事之尤至，將為盜，必卜之。

translations.literal: The custom of Raozhou favored spirits; there was the Jueshan Temple, which from old had been demonic and brought fortune and calamity upon men; robbers especially honored it, and before they would rob they always divined there.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou favored spirits. The Jueshan Temple had long been demonic, dispensing fortune and woe; robbers honored it above all and divined there before every raid.

sentences.zh: 鏞至，即撤其祠宇，沉土偶人於江。

translations.literal: When Yong arrived he at once demolished the shrine buildings and sank the clay images in the river.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Yong demolished the shrine and sank its clay images in the river.

sentences.zh: 凡境內淫祠有不合祀典者，皆毀之。

translations.literal: Every licentious shrine within the circuit that did not accord with the statutes of sacrifice was likewise destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Every illicit shrine in the circuit not authorized by the statutes of sacrifice was destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 人初大駭，已而皆嘆服。

translations.literal: At first the people were greatly alarmed; afterward all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people were alarmed; soon all admired him.

sentences.zh: 鏞知民可教，俾俊秀入學宮，求宿儒學行俱尊者，列為《五經》師，旦望必幅巾深衣以謁先聖，月必考訂課試，以示勸勵。

translations.literal: Yong knew the people could be taught; he had promising youths enter the school, sought elderly Confucians of respected learning and conduct, and appointed them teachers of the Five Classics; at dawn and dusk he always wore plain headcloth and deep robes to pay homage to the Sage; each month he set examinations and reviews to encourage study.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the people could be taught, he sent promising youths to the school, found venerable Confucians of learning and conduct, and made them teachers of the Five Classics. At dawn and dusk he wore plain cap and deep robes to salute the Sage; each month he held examinations to encourage study.

sentences.zh: 每治政之暇，必延見其師生，與之講討經義，由是人人自力於學，而饒之以科第進者，視他郡為多。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure from government he would summon teachers and students and discuss the classics with them; thereby everyone strove in learning for himself, and those of Raozhou who advanced through the examinations were more numerous than in other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure from government he summoned teachers and students to discuss the classics; everyone strove in learning, and more men of Raozhou passed the examinations than in other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鏞居官廨，自奉淡泊，僚屬亦皆化之。

translations.literal: Yong resided in the government office; his own maintenance was plain and frugal, and his subordinates all were transformed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong lived at the yamen on plain fare, and his subordinates all followed his example.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝使至外郡者，官府奉之甚侈，一不厭其所欲，即銜之，往往騰謗於朝，其出使於饒者，鏞延見郡舍中，供以糲飯，退皆無有後言。

translations.literal: Before this, when court envoys came to outer circuits, the local governments entertained them very lavishly; if they were not satisfied with their desires they harbored resentment and often spread slander at court. Those sent on mission to Raozhou—Yong received them at the prefectural lodging and supplied coarse rice; on departing none had further complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, court envoys to the provinces were entertained lavishly; if their wishes were not met they nursed grievances and often slandered officials at court. Envoys to Raozhou were received by Yong at the prefectural hostel and given coarse fare—and left without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 其後有旨以織幣脆薄，遣使笞行省臣及諸郡長吏。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict because woven currency was flimsy and thin, dispatching envoys to flog members of the Branch Secretariat and chief officials of the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict blamed inferior woven currency and sent envoys to flog provincial secretaries and circuit chiefs.

sentences.zh: 獨鏞無預。

translations.literal: Only Yong was not involved.
translations.idiomatic: Yong alone was not implicated.

sentences.zh: 鏞治政，雖細事，其詳密多類此。

translations.literal: In Yong's governance, even in small matters, his thoroughness was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Even in small matters, Yong governed with the same meticulous care.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became associate administrator of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丞相脫脫在位，而龔伯璲輩方用事，朝廷悉議更張，鏞有言，不見聽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chancellor Toktoghan was in power, while men like Gong Bolin were in ascendance; the court widely debated reforms. Yong spoke but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, with Toktoghan as chancellor and men like Gong Bolin in power, the court debated sweeping reforms. Yong objected, but no one listened.

sentences.zh: 人或以鏞優於治郡，而執政非其所長，遂出為甘肅行省參知政事。

translations.literal: Some held that Yong excelled at governing circuits but that holding high office was not his strength; he was therefore sent out as Associate Administrator of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Yong was better at governing a circuit than at central politics; he was posted as associate administrator of the Gansu branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及脫脫罷，用事者悉誅，而鏞又獨免禍。

translations.literal: When Toktoghan was dismissed, those in power were all executed, yet Yong alone again escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Toktoghan fell, his faction was wiped out—yet Yong alone escaped harm again.

sentences.zh: 乃遷西行台中丞，歿於官。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Western Branch Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the western branch secretariat and died in office.

sentences.zh: ○李稷

translations.literal: ○ Li Ji
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji

sentences.zh: 李稷，字孟豳，滕州人。

translations.literal: Li Ji, style name Mengbin, was a native of Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji (Mengbin) came from Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 稷幼穎敏，八歲能記誦經史。

translations.literal: Ji in youth was sharp and clever; at eight he could memorize the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Ji was exceptionally bright; at eight he could recite the classics and histories from memory.

sentences.zh: 從其父官袁州，師夏鎮，又從官鉛山，師方回孫。

translations.literal: He followed his father in office to Yuanzhou and studied under Xia Zhen; he again followed him to Qianshan and studied under Fang Huisun.
translations.idiomatic: When his father served at Yuanzhou, Ji studied under Xia Zhen; when he moved to Qianshan, Ji studied under Fang Huisun.

sentences.zh: 鎮、回孫皆名進士，長於《春秋》，稷兼得其傳。

translations.literal: Zhen and Huisun were both renowned jinshi, skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals; Ji received the transmission from both.
translations.idiomatic: Both Xia Zhen and Fang Huisun were distinguished jinshi and masters of the Spring and Autumn; Ji learned from each.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，中進士第，授淇州判官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Prefect of Qizhou.
