translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 4 he passed the jinshi examination and became assistant prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 淇當要衝，稷至，能理其劇。

translations.literal: Qizhou stood on a vital thoroughfare; when Ji arrived he could handle its arduous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou lay on a major route; Ji took office and managed its heavy workload with ease.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，告於朝堂以賑之，民獲以蘇。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine he reported to the court hall to obtain relief, and the people were able to recover.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe famine he petitioned the court for relief, and the people survived.

sentences.zh: 遊民尚安兒，飲博亡賴，稷疑其為非，督弓兵擒之，果盜鄰村王甲家財，與其黨五人俱伏辜。

translations.literal: A vagrant named Shang An'er, given to drink and gambling and a worthless fellow—Ji suspected him of wrongdoing, supervised archers in seizing him, and indeed he had robbed the household wealth of Wang Jia in a neighboring village; he and his five accomplices all paid with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: A drifter named Shang An'er lived by drink, dice, and petty crime. Ji suspected him, had archers seize him, and proved he had robbed a neighbor named Wang Jia; he and five accomplices were executed.

sentences.zh: 調海陵縣丞，亦有能聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Hailing County, where he likewise gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to assistant magistrate of Hailing County, he won the same reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為翰林國史院編修官，擢御史臺照磨。

translations.literal: He entered service as Compiler in the Hanlin Academy for National History and was promoted to Registry Clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a national-history compiler and rose to registry clerk of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 至正初，出為江南行台監察御史，遷都事，又入為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng he went out as Supervising Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was promoted to Chief Clerk, and again entered as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhizheng he served as supervising censor on the Jiangnan branch censorate, became chief clerk, then returned as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 劾奏閹宦高龍卜恃賴恩私，侵撓朝政，擅作威福，交通時相，請謁公行，為國基禍，乞加竄逐，以正邦刑。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the eunuch Gao Longbu, relying on private favor, encroached on court governance, arrogated authority, trafficked with the current chancellor, and made solicitations openly—bringing calamity on the state foundation—and begged that he be driven off to rectify the statutes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the eunuch Gao Longbu for abusing imperial favor, meddling in government, throwing his weight around, colluding with the chancellor, and taking bribes openly—acts that threatened the dynasty—and urged his banishment to restore the rule of law.

sentences.zh: 章上，流高龍卜於征東。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Gao Longbu was banished to the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted and Gao Longbu was exiled to the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 又言：「御史封事，須至御前開拆，以防壅蔽之患。

translations.literal: He also said: "Sealed memorials of censors must be opened only before the Emperor, to guard against the harm of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "Censors' sealed memorials must be opened only before the emperor, lest reports be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 言事官須優加擢用，以開諫諍之路。

translations.literal: Officials who speak must be specially promoted and employed, to open the path of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners who spoke truth to power should be promoted to keep the road of remonstrance open.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史、給事中、起居注，須任端人直士，書百司奏請，及帝所可否，月達省台，付史館，以備纂修之實。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censors, Remonstrance Officials, and Masters of the Diurnal Record must be men of upright character; they should record the memorials and requests of the hundred offices and what the Emperor approved or rejected, monthly reaching the Secretariat and Censorate and delivered to the History Office, to supply material for compilation in truth."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant censors, remonstrance officials, and diurnal recorders should be upright men who logged every ministry memorial and every imperial decision, sent monthly to the secretariat, censorate, and history office for the historical record."

sentences.zh: 承天護聖寺火，有旨更作，乃上言：「水旱相仍，公私俱乏，不宜妄興大役。」

translations.literal: When the Chengtian Huguosheng Temple burned, there was an edict to rebuild it; he then memorialized: "Floods and droughts follow one another; public and private stores alike are exhausted—it is not fitting rashly to undertake great works."
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Chengtian Huguosheng Temple, the court ordered rebuilding. Ji protested: "Flood and drought alternate; the treasury and the people are alike exhausted—this is no time for grand construction."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷方注意守令，因言：「下縣尹多從吏部銓注，或非其才，宜並歸省選。

translations.literal: As the court was then paying close attention to prefects and magistrates, he said: "Subordinate circuit magistrates are mostly appointed through the Ministry of Personnel; they are not always the right men—it would be better to return selection entirely to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With the court focused on local officials, he urged, "District magistrates, too often misfits from the Ministry of Personnel, should be chosen by the provinces instead.

sentences.zh: 茶鹽鐵課，責備長吏，動受刑譴，何以臨民，宜分委佐貳。

translations.literal: Tea, salt, and iron levies are charged to chief officials, who constantly suffer corporal punishment—how can they govern the people? The burden should be divided among deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Tea, salt, and iron taxes fell on chief officials, who were flogged for shortfalls—how could they govern? He urged shifting that burden to deputies.

sentences.zh: 投下達魯花赤，蠹政害民，宜為佐貳。」

translations.literal: Darugachi of invested appanages ruin government and harm the people; they should be made deputies."
translations.idiomatic: Darugachi on imperial estates corrupted government and oppressed the people; they too should be reduced to deputy rank."

sentences.zh: 帝悉可其奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷中書左司都事，又四遷為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Left Department of the Central Secretariat, and after four more promotions became Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk of the left secretariat department, then after four more steps became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廷議以中原租稅不實，將履畝起稅，稷詣都堂言曰：「方今妖寇竊發，民庶流亡，此政一行，是驅民為盜也。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the court debated that land rents in the Central Plains were not reported truly and would impose tax by measured acreage; Ji went to the chief councilors and said: "At present bandits and rebels are rising everywhere and the people are fleeing; if this policy is enacted, it will drive the people to become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the court planned to tax the Central Plains by measured acreage because rents were underreported. Ji told the chancellors: "Rebels roam the land and people flee; enact this and you will make bandits of them all."

sentences.zh: 相臣是之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋參議中書省事，俄遷治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Counselor of the Central Secretariat; shortly he was promoted to Investigating Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a secretariat counselor, then investigating attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從丞相脫脫出師徵徐州，徐既平，謁告歸滕州，遷曾祖父以下十七喪，序昭穆以葬，敕賜碑樹焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Chancellor Toktoghan on campaign to subdue Xuzhou; when Xu was pacified he requested leave and returned to Tengzhou, moved the coffins of seventeen deceased from his great-grandfather downward, arranged them in zhao-mu order for burial, and received an imperial edict granting a stele and trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he marched with Toktoghan to take Xuzhou. After the city fell he took leave, returned to Tengzhou, reburied seventeen ancestors from his great-grandfather down in proper order, and received an imperial stele and planted trees.

sentences.zh: 既而召為詹事丞，除侍御史，俄遷中書參知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, appointed Attendant Censor, and shortly promoted to Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the heir apparent's household, made attendant censor, then associate administrator of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇太子受冊，攝大禮使，遂除樞密副使。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent received his investiture, Ji served as acting Grand Master of Ceremonies and was then appointed Vice Minister of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the heir apparent's investiture he acted as grand master of ceremonies, then became vice minister of the privy council.

sentences.zh: 帝躬祀郊廟，攝太常少卿，尋復為侍御史，又為中書參知政事，俄升資善大夫、御史中丞，尋特加榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally sacrificed at the suburban altars, Ji served as acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon he was again Attendant Censor, again Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat, shortly raised to Senior Grand Master of Governance and Censor-in-Chief, and soon specially granted Grand Master of Glory and Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sacrificed at the suburban altars, Ji acted as vice director of imperial sacrifices, then returned as attendant censor and associate administrator, rose to senior grand master of governance and censor-in-chief, and was soon granted the title grand master of glory and blessings.

sentences.zh: 至正十九年，丁母憂，兩起復，為陝西行省左丞、樞密副使，乞終制，不起。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhizheng he mourned his mother; twice summoned back to service as Left Counselor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and Vice Minister of the Privy Council, he begged to complete mourning and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 19 he mourned his mother. Twice recalled as left counselor of the Shaanxi branch and vice minister of the privy council, he refused until mourning was complete.

sentences.zh: 服闋，命為大都路總管，兼大興府尹，除副詹事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Chief Administrator of Dadu Circuit, concurrently Magistrate of Daxing, and dismissed as Deputy Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became chief administrator of Dadu Circuit and magistrate of Daxing, and left the deputy directorship of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，出為陝西行台中丞，未行，改山東廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he went out as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; before departing he was changed to Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was named vice censor-in-chief of Shaanxi but, before he left, was reassigned as Shandong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 得疾，上章致仕，還京師。

translations.literal: He fell ill, submitted a memorial to retire, and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to retire; he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠贊理正憲功臣、集賢大學士、榮祿大夫、柱國，追封齊國公，諡文穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty and Upholds Rectitude, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Grand Master of Glory and Blessings, and Pillar of the State; enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with the posthumous name Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made meritorious minister of loyal rectitude, academician of the hall of gathered worthies, grand master of glory and blessings, and pillar of the state; enfeoffed as Duke of Qi with the posthumous name Wenmu ("Cultured and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 稷為人孝友恭儉，廉慎忠勤，處家嚴而有則，與人交，一以誠恪，尤篤於鄉黨朋友之誼。

translations.literal: Ji as a man was filial, friendly, respectful, and frugal, loyal, cautious, and diligent; at home he was strict yet principled; in dealing with others he was wholly sincere and respectful, especially devoted to the obligations of village and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was filial, cordial, frugal, loyal, and diligent—strict yet principled at home, wholly sincere with others, and especially devoted to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 中丞任擇善、陳思謙既沒，皆撫其遺孤，人以是多之。

translations.literal: After Vice Censor-in-Chief Ren Zeshan and Chen Siqian had died, he supported their orphaned children; people for this reason praised him the more.
translations.idiomatic: After Ren Zeshan and Chen Siqian died, he cared for their orphaned children—another reason contemporaries admired him.

sentences.zh: 出入台省者二十年，始卒無疵，為時名卿雲。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the censorate and secretariat for twenty years, from beginning to end without blemish, he was a famed minister of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years in the censorate and secretariat left him without a stain; he was counted among the age's great ministers.

sentences.zh: ○蓋苗

translations.literal: ○ Gai Miao
translations.idiomatic: Gai Miao

sentences.zh: 蓋苗，字耘夫，大名元城人。

translations.literal: Gai Miao, style name Yunfu, was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Miao (Yunfu) came from Yuancheng in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏好學，善記誦，及弱冠，遊學四方，藝業大進。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of learning, good at memorization; when he reached manhood he traveled to study in all directions and his arts advanced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and bookish as a boy, he traveled widely in early manhood and mastered his studies.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，登進士第，授濟寧路單州判官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Prefect of Shan County in Jining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 5 he passed the jinshi and became assistant prefect of Shan County in Jining Circuit.

sentences.zh: 州多系囚，苗請疏決之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had many prisoners held long in detention; Miao requested a general review and release.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture held many long-term prisoners; Miao petitioned for a mass review.

sentences.zh: 知州以為囚數已上，部使者未報，不可決。

translations.literal: The prefect said that the prisoner count had already been reported upward and the circuit envoy had not replied—it could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect refused: the caseload was already reported and the circuit envoy had not approved a review.

sentences.zh: 苗曰：「設使者有問，請身任其責。」

translations.literal: Miao said: "If the envoy should question it, let me bear the responsibility myself."
translations.idiomatic: Miao said, "If the envoy objects, let me answer for it."

sentences.zh: 知州乃勉從之，使者果閱牘而去。

translations.literal: The prefect then reluctantly consented; the envoy indeed examined the records and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect relented; the envoy reviewed the dockets and left satisfied.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，白郡府，未有以應。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he reported to the circuit government, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he appealed to the circuit government and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 會他邑亦以告，郡府遣苗至戶部以請，戶部難之，苗伏中書堂下，出糠餅以示曰：「濟寧民率食此，況不得此食者尤多，豈可坐視不救乎！」

translations.literal: When another county likewise reported, the circuit government sent Miao to the Ministry of Revenue to petition; the ministry made difficulties; Miao prostrated himself beneath the central secretariat hall, produced bran cakes and showed them, saying: "The people of Jining mostly eat this; how much more those who cannot even obtain this food—can we sit and watch without saving them!"
translations.idiomatic: When a neighboring county reported famine too, the circuit sent Miao to the Ministry of Revenue. The ministry balked; Miao knelt in the secretariat courtyard, held up bran cakes, and said, "This is what Jining's people eat—and many have not even this. Can we do nothing?"

sentences.zh: 因泣下，時宰大悟，凡被災者，咸獲賑焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept; the chief ministers were greatly awakened, and all who had suffered disaster alike received relief.
translations.idiomatic: He wept; the chancellors were moved, and every stricken region received relief.

sentences.zh: 有官粟五百石陳腐，以藉諸民，期秋熟還官。

translations.literal: There were five hundred shi of government grain grown moldy; he lent it to the people on the promise that when autumn ripened they would repay the government.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred shi of moldy government grain he lent to the people, to be repaid after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 及秋，郡責償甚急，部使者將責知州，苗曰：「官粟實苗所貰，今民飢不能償，苗請代還。」

translations.literal: When autumn came the circuit urgently demanded repayment; the circuit envoy was about to blame the prefect; Miao said: "The government grain was in truth borrowed by me; now the people are starving and cannot repay—I beg to repay in their stead."
translations.idiomatic: Come autumn the circuit demanded repayment and would punish the prefect. Miao said, "I borrowed that grain; the people are starving and cannot repay—let me make good the debt."

sentences.zh: 使者乃已其責。

translations.literal: The envoy then ceased the demand.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy dropped the case.

sentences.zh: 單州稅糧，歲輸館陶倉，距單五百餘里，載馱擔負，民甚苦之，春猶未足。

translations.literal: Shan County's tax grain each year was transported to the Guantao granary, more than five hundred li from Shan; by cart, pack animal, and shoulder pole the people suffered greatly, and even in spring the quota was not yet met.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Shan County's tax grain went to the Guantao granary five hundred li away—by cart, mule, and back—and spring would come before the quota was filled.

sentences.zh: 是秋，館陶大熟，苗先期令民糴粟倉下，十月初，倉券已至，省民力什之五。

translations.literal: That autumn Guantao had a great harvest; Miao beforehand ordered the people to buy grain below the granary; in the tenth month the warehouse receipts had arrived, saving the people five-tenths of their labor.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Guantao had a bumper crop; Miao had the people buy grain there in advance. By the tenth month the receipts were in hand, sparing the people half their usual toil.

sentences.zh: 辟御史臺掾，除山東廉訪司經歷，歷禮部主事，擢江南行台監察御史。

translations.literal: He was recruited as Clerk of the Censorate, appointed Intendant of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, served as Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was promoted to Supervising Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited to the censorate, he became Shandong surveillance intendant, a director in the Ministry of Rites, then supervising censor on the Jiangnan branch.

sentences.zh: 建言嚴武備以備不虞，簡兵卒以壯國勢，全功臣以隆大體，惜官爵以清銓選，考實行以抑奔競，明賞罰以杜姦欺，計利害以孚民情，去民賊以崇禮節。

translations.literal: He memorialized to tighten military preparedness against the unforeseen, streamline soldiers to strengthen the state's power, preserve meritorious ministers to uphold great principle, cherish official ranks to clarify selection, examine actual conduct to restrain frantic competition, clarify rewards and punishments to stop deceit, calculate benefit and harm to win the people's hearts, and remove oppressors of the people to exalt ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He urged stricter defense, leaner armies, honor for meritorious ministers, restraint in appointments, merit over ambition, clear rewards and punishments, policies weighed for the people's sake, and the removal of local tyrants—all timely counsel, widely praised.

sentences.zh: 皆切於時務，公論韙之。

translations.literal: All were close to the needs of the time; public opinion approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion endorsed every point.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，文宗詔以建康潛邸為佛寺，務窮壯麗，毀民居七十餘家，仍以御史大夫督其役。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansli, Emperor Wenzong ordered that the Jianye princely residence be made a Buddhist temple, striving for utmost grandeur and splendor, demolishing more than seventy households of common people, and again had the Censor-in-Chief supervise the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiansli, Emperor Wenzong turned his former Jianye residence into a Buddhist temple of extravagant scale, razing more than seventy homes and putting the censor-in-chief in charge of construction.

sentences.zh: 苗上封事曰：「臣聞使民以時，使臣以禮，自古未有不由斯道而致隆平者。

translations.literal: Miao submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that employing the people at the proper seasons and employing ministers with propriety—from antiquity none who failed to follow this path attained great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Miao submitted a sealed memorial: "I have heard that rulers who use the people in season and treat ministers with ritual have always found peace—none who ignored this road did.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍潛建業之時，居民困於供給，幸而獲睹今日之運，百姓跂足舉首，以望非常之恩。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was in dragon exile at Jianye, the residents were distressed by supplies; fortunate to behold today's fortune, the hundred surnames stand on tiptoe and raise their heads, looking for extraordinary grace.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty lived in Jianye as prince, the people strained to supply you. Now they stand on tiptoe for extraordinary grace.

sentences.zh: 今奪農時以創佛寺，又廢民居，使之家破產盪，豈聖人禦天下之道乎？

translations.literal: Now you seize the farming season to create a Buddhist temple and again demolish residences, making families ruined and destitute—is this the way of a sage in ruling all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you seize the farming season to build a temple and tear down homes, ruining families—is this how a sage rules the realm?

sentences.zh: 昔漢高帝興於豐、沛，為復兩縣，光武中興南陽，免稅三年，既不務此，而隆重佛氏，何以滿斯民之望哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han rose at Feng and Pei and exempted those two counties; Emperor Guangwu at the restoration of Nanyang exempted taxes for three years—if you do not attend to this but instead honor Buddhism, how can you satisfy the people's hopes?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu exempted Feng and Pei; Guangwu freed Nanyang from tax for three years. If you ignore that precedent and lavish honor on Buddhism, how will you meet the people's hopes?

sentences.zh: 且佛以慈悲為心，方便為教，今尊佛氏而害生民，無乃違其方便之教乎？

translations.literal: Moreover Buddhism takes compassion as its heart and expedience as its teaching—now honoring Buddhism while harming living people, is this not contrary to its teaching of expedience?
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism teaches compassion and expedience—yet you honor the faith by harming the people. Does that not betray its own teaching?

sentences.zh: 台臣職專糾察，表正百司，今乃委以修繕之役，豈其禮哉？」

translations.literal: Censors' duty is devoted to investigation and correction, setting right the hundred offices—now to entrust them with repair labor, is this their propriety?"
translations.idiomatic: Censors exist to correct officials, not to supervise construction—is this proper work for them?"

sentences.zh: 書奏，御史大夫果免督役。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Censor-in-Chief was indeed relieved of supervising the labor.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was accepted and the censor-in-chief was relieved of the project.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 文宗幸護國仁王寺，泛舟玉泉，苗進曰：「今頻年不登，邊隅不靖，政當恐懼修省，何暇逸遊，以臨不測之淵乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong visited the Huguo Renwang Temple and boated on the Jade Spring, Miao advanced and said: "For years harvests have failed and the frontiers are unsettled—government should fear and cultivate itself; what leisure for roaming pleasure, to approach an unfathomable abyss?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong visited the Huguo Renwang Temple and rowed on the Jade Spring, Miao said, "Harvests fail and the borders are uneasy—you should be in fear and self-cultivation, not at play beside an abyss."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之，賜以對衣上尊，即日還宮。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it, bestowing matching robes and fine wine; that same day he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, gave him court robes and wine, and returned to the palace the same day.

sentences.zh: 台臣擬苗僉淮東廉訪司事，以聞，帝曰：「仍留蓋御史，朕欲聞其讜言也。」

translations.literal: The censors proposed Miao as Commissioner of the Huaidong Surveillance Commission and reported it; the Emperor said: "Let Censor Gai remain—I wish to hear his forthright words."
translations.idiomatic: The censors nominated him for Huaidong surveillance commissioner; the emperor said, "Keep Censor Gai—I want his blunt counsel."

sentences.zh: 以丁外艱去，免喪，除太禧宗禋院都事。

translations.literal: He left on mourning for his father; when mourning ended he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Temple for Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: He left to mourn his father; after mourning he became chief clerk of the grand temple for imperial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 中書檄苗行視河道，還言：「河口淤塞，今苟不治，後日必為中原大患。」

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat dispatched Miao to inspect the river course; on returning he said: "The river mouth is silted and blocked—if it is not managed now, later it will surely become a great calamity for the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat sent him to inspect the waterways. He reported, "The river mouth is choked with silt; neglect it now and the Central Plains will suffer."

sentences.zh: 都水難之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Waterways made difficulties; the matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The waterways office objected, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 至正初，用薦者知亳州，修學宮，完州廨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng, on recommendation he became Prefect of Bozhou, repaired the school, and completed the prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhizheng, recommended for office, he became prefect of Bozhou, restored the school, and rebuilt the yamen.

sentences.zh: 有豪強佔民田為己業，民五十餘人訴於苗，苗訊治之，豪民咸自引服。

translations.literal: Powerful families had seized commoners' fields as their own property; more than fifty people sued Miao; Miao investigated and tried the case, and the powerful all confessed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Local magnates had seized peasants' land; more than fifty plaintiffs came to Miao, who investigated until every offender confessed.

sentences.zh: 苗曰：「爾等罪甚重，然吾觀皆有改過意。」

translations.literal: Miao said: "Your crimes are very grave, yet I observe you all have the intention to reform."
translations.idiomatic: Miao said, "Your crimes are grave, but I see you mean to amend."

sentences.zh: 遂從輕議。

translations.literal: He then judged leniently.
translations.idiomatic: He sentenced them lightly.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，起為左司都事，在左司僅十八日，凡決數百事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he was raised to Chief Clerk of the Left Department; in the Left Department for only eighteen days he decided several hundred matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 he became chief clerk of the left department and, in eighteen days there, disposed of hundreds of cases.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂，宰相惜其去，重賻之。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; the chancellor regretted his departure and gave him a heavy parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died the chancellor regretted losing him and sent a generous farewell gift.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，起為戶部郎中，俄擢御史臺都事，御史大夫欲以故人居言路，苗曰：「非其才也。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was raised to Director in the Ministry of Revenue; shortly he was promoted to Chief Clerk of the Censorate; the Censor-in-Chief wished to place an old acquaintance on the remonstrance path; Miao said: "He is not the right man."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 2 he became a revenue director, then chief censorate clerk. When the censor-in-chief wanted a friend on the remonstrance staff, Miao said, "He is not fit."

sentences.zh: 大夫不悅而起，其晚，邀至私第以謝，人兩賢之。

translations.literal: The chief minister rose displeased; that evening he invited him to his private residence to apologize; people praised both men.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief stalked off angry; that evening he invited Miao home to apologize—contemporaries admired them both.

sentences.zh: 出為山東廉訪副使。

translations.literal: He went out as Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as deputy Shandong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 益都、淄、萊地舊稱產金，朝廷建一府六所綜其事，民歲買金以輸官，至是六十年矣。

translations.literal: Yidu, Zi, and Lai districts were formerly said to produce gold; the court established one office and six bureaus to oversee the matter; the people each year bought gold to deliver to the government—for this it had been sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu, Zi, and Lai were famed for gold; the court ran one office and six bureaus, and for sixty years the people had bought gold to pay the state.

sentences.zh: 民有忤其官長意，輒謂所居地有金礦，掘地及泉而後止。

translations.literal: If a commoner offended his official superior, they would say his dwelling sat on a gold mine, dig the ground until reaching springs, and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: Offend a local official and he would declare your home sat atop a gold mine, dig until he hit water, then stop.

sentences.zh: 猾吏為奸利，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Crafty clerks made illicit profit; none dared call them to account.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks profited; no one dared challenge them.

sentences.zh: 苗建言罷之。

translations.literal: Miao memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Miao petitioned to abolish the system.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，由都水監遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he moved from Director of Waterways to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he rose from director of waterways to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 初，盜殺河南省憲官，延坐五百餘家，已有詔除首罪外，餘從原宥。

translations.literal: At first, when bandits killed a surveillance official of Henan Province, more than five hundred households were implicated by extension; there was already an edict that apart from the chief culprits the rest were to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after robbers killed a Henan surveillance official, guilt by association had swept in more than five hundred families; an edict had already spared all but the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 至是，宰臣追复欲盡誅戮，苗堅持不可。

translations.literal: At this time the chief ministers pursued the matter again and wished to execute everyone; Miao firmly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: By then the chief ministers wanted to reopen the case and put every implicated household to death; Miao stood firm against it.

sentences.zh: 御史趣具獄，苗曰：「肆赦复殺，在法所無，御史獨宜劾​​苗，其敢累朝廷之寬仁乎！」

translations.literal: The censor urged that the case be prepared; Miao said: "After a general amnesty to kill again—there is nothing of this in the law; the censor alone ought to impeach Miao—how dare he burden the court's clemency!"
translations.idiomatic: The censor pressed to finalize the prosecution. Miao said, "To grant a general amnesty and then execute again has no place in law. The censor should impeach me alone—how dare anyone burden the court's mercy!"

sentences.zh: 卒用苗議，罷之。

translations.literal: In the end they adopted Miao's proposal and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The court took Miao's advice and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 出為山東廉訪使，民飢為盜，所在群聚，乃上救荒弭盜十二事，劾宣慰使骫骳不法者。

translations.literal: He went out as Shandong Surveillance Commissioner; the people, starving, became bandits and gathered everywhere; he then submitted twelve measures to relieve famine and suppress banditry, and impeached Pacification Commissioners who were crooked and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Shandong surveillance commissioner, he found hungry people turning bandit in mass gatherings; he memorialized twelve famine-and-banditry remedies and impeached lawless pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 有司援例欲徵苗所得職田，苗曰：「年荒民困，吾無以救，尚忍徵斂以肥己耶！」

translations.literal: The responsible offices cited precedent wishing to levy Miao's received official fields; Miao said: "In years of famine the people are distressed; I have no means to save them—how can I still bear to levy taxes to enrich myself!"
translations.idiomatic: When officials cited precedent to collect his supervisor's allotment fields, Miao said, "The land is in famine and the people suffer; I cannot save them—how could I tax them to fatten myself?"

sentences.zh: 輒命已之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the levy halted at once.

sentences.zh: 同僚皆無敢取。

translations.literal: His colleagues all dared not take such levies.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues dared not collect either.

sentences.zh: 召參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to deliberate secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為陝西行台侍御史，遷陝西行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as Attending Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Associate Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became Shaanxi branch censor, then Shaanxi associate administrator.

sentences.zh: 六年，復入為治書侍御史，升侍御史，尋拜中書參知政事、同知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he reentered as Attending Secretary of the Secretariat for Filing, was promoted to Attending Censor, and soon appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat and Associate Director of the Classics Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he returned as supervising secretary-censor, rose to attending censor, then became secretariat associate administrator and classics lecturer.

sentences.zh: 大臣以兩京馳道狹隘，奏毀民田廬廣之，已遣使督有司治之矣，苗執曰：「馳道創自至元初，何今日獨為隘乎！」

translations.literal: Great ministers, because the imperial highways of the two capitals were narrow, memorialized to destroy commoners' fields and houses to widen them; they had already sent envoys to oversee the responsible offices in carrying it out; Miao insisted: "The imperial highway was created from the beginning of Zhiyuan—why today alone is it said to be narrow!"
translations.idiomatic: Ministers said the twin-capital expressways were too narrow and petitioned to raze homes and fields to widen them; envoys were already overseeing the work. Miao objected, "Those roads date to early Zhiyuan—why are they suddenly too narrow?"

sentences.zh: 力辯，乃罷。

translations.literal: He argued forcefully, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He argued fiercely until the project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又欲宿衛士悉出為郡長官，俾以養貧，苗議曰：「郡長所以牧民，豈養貧之地哉？

translations.literal: They also wished to send all palace guards out as prefectural chiefs to support the poor thereby; Miao disputed: "Prefects exist to shepherd the people—how could they be a place to support the poor?
translations.idiomatic: Another plan would make every guardsman a prefect to relieve poverty. Miao said, "Prefects govern the people—they are not welfare posts.

sentences.zh: 果有不能自存，賜之錢可也。

translations.literal: If some truly cannot support themselves, giving them money would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If men truly cannot live, give them money.

sentences.zh: 若任郡寄，必擇賢才而後可。」

translations.literal: If one entrusts prefectural responsibility, one must choose worthy talent before it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: County office must go only to the worthy."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又欲以鈔萬貫與角牴者，苗曰：「諸處告飢，不蒙賑恤，力戲何功，獲此重賞乎？」

translations.literal: They also wished to give ten thousand strings of paper money to wrestlers; Miao said: "Everywhere reports famine yet receives no relief—what merit has strength-play to win such a heavy reward!"
translations.idiomatic: They also meant to grant ten thousand strings of notes to wrestlers. Miao said, "Regions starve without relief—what merit does wrestling show to earn such a prize?"

sentences.zh: 又，僉四川廉訪司事家人違例收職田，奉使宣撫，直坐其主，宰臣命奉使即行遣，苗請付法司詳議，勿使憲司以為口實。

translations.literal: Also, an acting Sichuan surveillance commissioner's household had irregularly collected official fields; the pacification envoy blamed the commissioner directly; the chief minister ordered the envoy to dismiss him immediately; Miao requested to hand it to the judicial offices for detailed deliberation, lest the surveillance offices have cause for complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In another case a Sichuan surveillance commissioner's household illegally took allotment fields; the pacification envoy punished the commissioner himself. When ministers ordered immediate dismissal, Miao asked that the law offices decide the case so the surveillance corps would not gain a grievance.

sentences.zh: 於是時相顧謂僚佐曰：「所以引蓋君至樞機者，欲其相助也，乃每事相抗，何耶？

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief minister of the time turned and said to his aides: "The reason for bringing Master Gai into the pivot of power was to have him assist—yet on every matter he resists—why?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister then told his staff, "We brought Gai into the inner councils to help—not to oppose us on everything. Why does he?

sentences.zh: 今後有公務，毋白參政。」

translations.literal: Henceforth for public affairs, do not report to the Associate Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: Report no official business to the associate administrator from now on."

sentences.zh: 苗歎曰：「猥以非才，待罪執政，中書之事，皆當與聞，今宰相言若此，不退何俟？」

translations.literal: Miao sighed and said: "I humbly with unfit talent bear punishment in governing; all Central Secretariat affairs ought to be heard by me—now the chancellor speaks thus—what am I waiting for if I do not withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: Miao sighed, "Unworthy as I am, I still share the administration; secretariat affairs are mine to hear. If the chancellor says this, why should I stay?"

sentences.zh: 將引去，而適有旨拜江南行台御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was about to withdraw, when just then an order appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was leaving when an edict named him Jiangnan vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 然宰臣怒苗終不解，比至，即除甘肅行省左丞，時苗已致仕歸田裡矣。

translations.literal: Yet the chief minister's anger at Miao was never resolved; when he arrived, he was immediately appointed Left Associate Administrator of the Gansu Branch Secretariat—by then Miao had already retired to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's grudge never cooled; as soon as Miao arrived they named him Gansu left associate administrator—even though he had already retired home.

sentences.zh: 時宰復奏旨趣赴任，苗舁疾就道。

translations.literal: The chief minister of the time again memorialized an order urging him to take up the post; Miao, carried in a litter, took the road.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor pressed another edict for him to report; Miao went, borne on a litter.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，即上言：「西土諸王，為國籓屏，賜賚雖有常制，而有司牽於文法，遂使恩澤不以時及，有匱乏之憂，大非隆親厚本之意。」

translations.literal: On reaching his post, he immediately submitted: "The princes of the western lands are the screen and shield of the state; largess though it has a regular rule, the offices are constrained by formal regulations, so that grace and favor do not reach in season, and there is the worry of want—greatly contrary to the intent of honoring kin and thickening the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: At his post he memorialized, "Western princes are the realm's bulwark. Though stipends follow fixed rules, bureaucrats bound by regulations delay them until princes face poverty—contrary to the policy of honoring kin."

sentences.zh: 又言：「甘肅每歲中糧，姦弊百端，請以糧鈔兼給，則軍民咸利矣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Gansu each year when distributing grain pay has a hundred kinds of fraud and abuse; I request that grain and paper money be given together—then army and people will all benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Gansu's annual grain deliveries are riddled with abuse; grain and notes should be paid together, to the profit of army and people alike."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西行御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi surveillance vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 到官數日，即上疏乞骸骨，還鄉里。

translations.literal: Within a few days of taking office he memorialized requesting his bones, and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Days after taking office he begged retirement and went home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈攄誠贊治功臣、中書左丞、上護軍，追封魏國公，諡文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Exerting-Sincerity Praising-Governance Meritorious Subject, Left Associate of the Central Secretariat, Senior Protector of the Army; was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, posthumous name Wénxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors named him Exerting Sincerity, Praising Governance merit subject, left secretariat associate, senior protector of the army, Duke of Wei, with the temple name Wenxian (Literary Offering).

sentences.zh: 苗學術淳正，性孝友，喜施與，置義田以贍宗族。

translations.literal: Miao's learning was pure and upright, his nature filial and fraternal, fond of giving; he established a charity field to support the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Miao's scholarship was upright, his nature dutiful and generous; he set up a charity estate for his kin.

sentences.zh: 平居恂恂謙謹，及至​​遇事，張目敢言，雖經挫折，無少回撓，有古遺直之風焉。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he was respectful and cautious; yet when it came to affairs he opened his eyes and dared speak; though he met setbacks, without the least bending back—he had the air of the ancient steadfastly straight.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was humble and cautious; in office he spoke boldly; setbacks never bent him—a throwback to the stubborn integrity of old.
